source.title: Drainage Master Plan for NCT of Delhi
source.publisher: IIT Delhi for the Irrigation and Flood Control Department, Government of NCT of Delhi
source.license_or_reuse_note: Use the report as a cited public reference; retain attribution and the report's scale and model limitations.

scope.pilot_alignment: Basin-wide information; no surveyed Dwarka Mor subcatchment boundary is supplied by these figures.
scope.notice: This report context is not a live observation, current pilot boundary, measured depth dataset, or calibrated input to the Dwarka forecast model.

terrain.use_limit: Basin-scale 2018 DEM context only; it does not provide surveyed street elevations or the pilot graph's vertical datum.

land_use.use_limit: The broad Urban land-use share is not a measured impervious percentage and must not be substituted for a local runoff coefficient.

drainage_context.network_description: The report describes a connected storm-drain network maintained by multiple agencies.
basin_features: water bodies and local low areas
drainage_context.map_limit: These are basin-scale report figures, not coordinate tables. Figure 3.3-7 describes reported waterlogging locations, not measured depth observations; map points should not be treated as exact GPS coordinates.

reported_flood_mechanisms.label: Low-point storage
reported_flood_mechanisms.description: Runoff collects in local depressions during rain and can remain congested.

reported_flood_mechanisms.label: Upstream inflow
reported_flood_mechanisms.description: Some trunk drains carry stormwater originating outside Delhi, adding flow to the regional network.

reported_flood_mechanisms.label: Pump and downstream interaction
reported_flood_mechanisms.description: Pump failure can worsen local congestion; pumping surplus water into a nearby drain can load downstream reaches.

reported_flood_mechanisms.label: Storage and local infiltration
reported_flood_mechanisms.description: The report explores routing runoff to water bodies, parks, permeable pavement, and rain gardens as modeled mitigation scenarios.

simulation_evidence.rainfall_reference: Palam station design rainfall; scenario input, not a live forecast
simulation_evidence.input_quality_note: The report says department survey data supplied for the initial scenario had not been properly vetted. Scenario values are model outputs, not observed flood measurements; storage depths are assumptions. The report labels one result as nodes and another as junctions, so the counts are shown separately rather than as a direct before/after score.
simulation_evidence.network_effect_note: The report says correcting drain slopes can move flooding upstream or downstream, so mitigation should be assessed across connected reaches.

safe_uses: Explain why local depressions, upstream loading, pump availability, and receiving-drain capacity matter.
Guide future graph fields for surveyed outfalls, pump controls, storage assets, and connected subcatchments.
Show basin-wide land-use context with explicit scale and source labels.
requires_local_verification_before_model: Dwarka subcatchment boundary and flow direction
drain connectivity, slope, dimensions, and capacity
pump locations, capacities, operating state, and receiving reach
water-body or park storage capacity and inlet/outlet connectivity
local land-cover fractions and runoff parameters
